content:
**Observations:**

- **Affected part**: Stem/crown and root system — two specimens pulled from soil, showing the base of the plant
- **Crown area**: Significant brown to dark-brown rot/decay at the soil line, with disintegrated tissue
- **Stem**: Lower stem shows bleached/whitish-tan tissue with brown streaking; some fibrous material around the crown (possible mycelium)
- **Roots**: Brown, dead, and matted — classic soilborne root death
- **Upper stem**: Still green above the affected zone, suggesting crown-level girdling

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii): Crown rot at soil line, bleached stem tissue, root death — fits well. White mycelial mat and small round sclerotia are hallmarks but may not be visible in this view or stage.
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Can cause crown/root rot with dark brown lesions, but lesions are typically more water-soaked and discrete.
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Causes internal vascular browning more than external crown rot of this severity.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: Would show white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia — not evident here.
- **Bacterial Wilt variants**: Primarily vascular/systemic wilting, not this type of external crown decay.

The bleached lower stem, brown crown rot at soil line, and dead root system are most characteristic of **Southern Blight**.
